subject: Prod: elevated p99 for Hosted API — client SDK timeouts suspected
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@quickcommerce.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Prod impact — spikes in p99 and 5xxs across token-generation endpoint

Hi Dylan & Marissa,

We started seeing a significant uptick in checkout failures this morning around 08:45 PST. Our metrics show token-generation calls to your hosted endpoint are spiking at p99 (~1.6s -> 4.8s) and we're observing a correlated increase in 5xx error rate across regions. This is affecting ~12% of our purchase flows and causing checkout retries on our side.

Important context:
- We use the Redwood JS SDK v1.3.2 with a client timeout of 2s and aggressive retries.
- Error IDs sample: 7f3b2c, 7f3b2e, 7f3b41 (I can share more).
- We see bursts from a small number of IPs during the window.

Can you confirm whether this is a backend regression or something on our side? We need a quick mitigation — customers are seeing declined checkouts.

Attaching a CSV of a replay trace and a screenshot of errors.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Engineering 
QuickCommerce

Samir — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I'm escalating immediately.

Quick next steps while we investigate:
- Can you share 3-5 representative request IDs and timestamps (you already gave a few; more helps).
- As an immediate mitigation, please try increasing the SDK request timeout from 2s to 8–10s and temporarily reduce retries (or add exponential backoff with jitter). We've seen client-side timeouts + aggressive retries magnify transient server latency.
- I'll loop in infra (Sergio) to validate backend telemetry and correlate with your request IDs.

I'll host a short sync at 10:00 PT if that works for your team — want to align on rollback/mitigation.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks

Thanks for flagging — I pulled traces and request logs for 08:30–09:30 PST. Initial findings:

- Server-side: p50/p95 show small bumps (p95 ~ 220ms -> 340ms) but not the ~4s p99 Samir reported.
- Customer-observed p99: many of the 4–5s tails appear to be client-side timeouts and retry cascades. We see a high rate of immediate retries (<=200ms) from the same client Request-IDs which line up with Samir's replay logs.
- Error attribution: ~83% of observed 5xxs in the window are immediately preceded by a client 408/timeout on the same Request-ID from QuickCommerce. In other words, clients time out, retry, and amplify load which then causes stochastic 5xxs under bursty conditions.

I attached a sampled CSV of replay traces (quickcommerce-replay-logs-0304.csv) and a short query result. Key datapoints:
- 2027-03-04T08:47:21Z: Request abc123 first attempt 1.9s, client timed out at 2s and retried 3x within 1s -> server returned 503 on subsequent attempts.
- Peak concurrent inflight requests from QuickCommerce IP range: 14 (steady baseline ~2).

Immediate recommendations:
1) Customer: increase client request timeout to >=8s, add jittered exponential backoff, and enable client-side de-duplication if possible.
2) Us: temporarily raise soft concurrency throttles for QuickCommerce (we can do this per-tenant for 30m window) to avoid 503s while they iterate.
3) Engineering follow-up: add server-side smoothing to reject obvious retry floods earlier and surface a clear Retry-After header.

I'll stand by on the 10:00 PT call and can provide a packet of raw traces.

-Sergio
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Prod impact — spikes in p99 and 5xxs across token-generation endpoint

Thanks — we applied the following at 11:40 PST as an emergency change:
- SDK timeout increased from 2s -> 8s
- Retries disabled for token-generation calls (we'll re-introduce with backoff/jitter next week)

Early results: error rate on our checkout path dropped by ~70% within 10 minutes. We're still monitoring but things look much healthier. I'll keep the 10:00 PT sync on the calendar for a technical postmortem.

One ask from my side: given the user impact and that the SDK default timeout of 2s contributed to the problem, can QuickCommerce get a goodwill credit for the impacted day? Please advise next steps.

-Samir

Appreciate the quick work here. Summary & decisions:

- Root cause (short): customer SDK default timeout + aggressive immediate retries caused a retry amplification pattern under a short-lived backend tail. Backend was not broadly degraded.
- Mitigation accepted: customer changed SDK timeout and reduced retries, and Engineering temporarily eased per-tenant throttles. Error rates recovered.

Decision: offer a one-week service credit equivalent to 10% of QuickCommerce's monthly invoice for March 2027 (Marissa — please prepare the credit and the customer note).

Action items & owners:
- Marissa Cole: send credit and customer-facing summary + postmortem.
- Sergio Alvarez / SRE: add server-side retry-smoothing and surface Retry-After header (P1 for next sprint).
- Developer Experience: update Redwood JS SDK default timeout to 8s and add a prominent note in the SDK README about safe retry patterns. (Dylan — can you coordinate with DevX on priority?)
- Dylan Brooks: follow up on comms and ensure the customer is satisfied.

I'll join any follow-up if needed. Good work triaging and getting this stabilized quickly.

-Rishi Malhotra
VP, Customer Success & GTM Ops
Redwood Inference
